S1.published:
I organize that adult capacity into three functions: Nurturer, Protector, and Leader/Guru. They aren’t three literal beings. They’re three ways the present-day person reparents the inner child.
(His inner child guide: "That’s one grown-up doing three jobs, not three more people moving in to help with the rent, and each job keeps the others in balance.")
S1.paragraph_after: Here I’m going to talk about what you develop in yourself as you reparent your inner child. I’m going to talk about it in terms of three jobs: your loving Nurturer, your safe Adult Protector (hereafter just the Protector) and your wise Guide. That’s one grown-up doing three jobs, not three more people moving in to help with the rent, and each job keeps the others in balance. It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.
S1.paragraph_before: Your inner child won’t trust you right away. It’s not going to be enough for you to meditate, say three nice sentences to the inner child and expect to have its trust. What’s going to help your inner child to trust you is you, the person you are right now, becoming reliable.
S1.paragraph_next: Also, your inner child’s worth is not dependent on these qualities… It has its own worth, and its own qualities, like playing, being tender, not taking life too seriously, being creative and wondering at the world. Those belong in your relationship with it too, not just the wounds.

S2.paragraph_before: The problem is that some people do not have access to their adult functions at will. Instead, they may go blank, access an inherited inner critic, or feel like a child part who may be playing at being an adult (what I call forced adulthood). Telling them to just access their adult is like telling a baby bird to just fly.
S2.paragraph_next: Access your witnessing position if necessary, just noticing what’s there, without needing it to be warm or wise or certain. If you already know how to access different internal positions, move immediately to accessing the adult position you want to borrow.

S3a.published: Choose a physically secure place without driving, water, machinery, or anyone needing your supervision. When intoxicated, acutely confused, or unable to keep yourself safe, deal with immediate support rather than exploratory hypnosis. The later Already open? practice is for orientation, not permission to intensify an unstable state.

S3a.note: sample ci, not cg: the meaning reader (REVIEW-A2.md) failed cg's "don't deepen if you can't be safe" as narrower than his "an unstable state" and its "you can use" for losing "is for orientation"; ci keeps "to help orient yourself" and "if you are not in a safe state"
S3a.paragraph_after: Put yourself in a place where you can safely do this. Don't do this if you're driving, in the water, operating machinery, or otherwise need to be attending to yourself or other people. If you are intoxicated, acutely confused, or not able to keep yourself safe, then get some immediate support instead of doing exploratory hypnosis. If you are already partially or fully opened, you can use the later 'Already open? Contain before you deepen' section to help orient yourself, but do not attempt to deepen yourself if you are not stable.
S3a.paragraph_before: Get clear on what it is you want to do during the induction. What do you want not to do today? How long do you want to spend on this? (You don't have to do this on a problem. You can do it on something you want to experience more of: love, play, confidence, creativity, communion, whatever.) Make sure you're leaving some time at the end to come back, and reflect on what you experienced.
S3a.paragraph_next: Deciding to do it. How will you coax yourself to do this? Make it spacious? Make it warm and held? Something else? Preview what you are going to do: will you close your eyes? Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end? If you are going to use a recording, read the script if you can. Remind yourself that if you say 'stop' at any time, the induction will end. If you say 'less', you will be asked to do less. If you say 'quiet', the talking will stop. You can also just open your eyes and stop, and then come all the way back anyway. You don't need to ask any parts for permission to stop, even if a part tells you that you do.

S6.published: Neither response establishes its origin. A protective part needn’t reveal its fear quickly; a comforting response doesn’t prove an interpretation either. The useful question is whether this way of responding helps you become clearer, steadier, and less hooked. Love and boundaries don’t require a verdict first.
S6.paragraph_after: You don’t have to find out if it’s a guard immediately, and you may not be able to comfort it quickly. Is this way of responding helping you to be clearer and steadier and less hooked?
S6.paragraph_before: If you feel vulnerable, if you feel tightness in your throat, if you feel sadness or fear or like you’re trying to protect something, call upon your Nurturer. If you don’t feel better, or if it continues being hostile towards you, stop trying to deal with it and return to your body and the room.
